promoting-suite · rung 4 · 2 flowsbudget 16.0m · budget > 1.5× p95 · lower to 9.0m
op-sqlite-probe android 4 no evidence — / 5.0m — A burst of five writes, each read back before the next, ALL survive process death on real flash. The Node boot-condition tier proves 52 of 56 cells against NodeSqliteDriver — an in-memory node:sqlite stand-in with no database file and no WAL to recover — so this is the only evidence in the repo about the engine the product actually ships. NOT a concurrency claim: Maestro drives one device serially and awaits each chunk's exit, so the writes cannot overlap the reads, and an earlier draft that claimed contention was wrong. NOT an exactly-once proof either: it detects an intent RE-EXECUTED on recovery (the row would sort ahead) but not a row duplicated verbatim, which needs a surface publishing a count.
share-intent-in android 4 no evidence — / 1.0m — A text share delivered from OUTSIDE the app (ACTION_SEND via the activity manager) opens Quick capture carrying the shared text verbatim. The payload half is the claim: ShareIntentIngest routes through centraid://capture?text=<encoded>, so a build that opened the right screen while mangling the text is a regression a screen-only assertion misses. Android only — iOS needs a second app to share from, which the lane does not install.
sharing · rung 4 · 1 flowsbudget 5.0m · budget > 1.5× p95 · lower to 4.5m
sharing-reach android 4 no evidence — / 3.0m — a person becomes shareable-with only by being LINKED, and the phone says so — the sheet opens, the linking surface loads, and offline the verb is withheld with its own sentence rather than offered and refused. If this passes when it should not, a release ships in which the mobile seat offers a share it cannot deliver.

Field observationsfrom QUALITY.md · 30 open

Things a lane noticed that no gate owns yet. Each entry ages until it becomes a law, a budget, or a closed issue; an observation older than 60 days is a rung-5 red.

  • A golden-corpus re-freeze cannot be read as a diff, and the freezer's own header says it should be.
  • `refreshEntityTriggers` refreshes a missing trigger, never a changed one.
  • Ten web e2e specs still carry a hand-copied connected-session bootstrap.
  • "Free up space" on mobile is a button that can never be pressed.
  • The comment-density ratchet does not measure what its header claims.
  • `portable-export.ts` keeps an append-only audit ledger in the State layer.
  • `evaluateReplicaRead` has no production caller on any host.
  • An ordered replica page cannot use an index while its refusal guards ride the same statement.
  • Two surfaces #882 added to the phone are unvirtualized.
  • The phone's Access history cannot narrow to one item.
  • Agenda's search field appears to stall while you type.
  • CI's Rust toolchain floats, so a clippy release can turn any branch red.
  • Banner-heavy modules are a size smell, not a comment smell.
  • Blueprint handler contracts live in inert JSDoc, not types.
  • Sub-wave stamps in test-name string literals.
  • `countDeclaredTests` counts prose.
  • Cheap gateway reads are starved by app-engine worker spawns under composition.
  • The desktop crash log is correct as a local file and wrong the moment anything shares it.
  • A place shared into an audience scope may be phrased against the wrong Home.
  • Two container-hermeticity defects found by an attempted in-container full coverage run
  • A packaged desktop cannot spawn its detached gateway, whatever the CLI path resolves to.
  • A retired entity left an inaccurate coverage comment behind.
  • `google-calendar-invite-send` uses wall-clock `new Date()`
  • `apps/desktop/tests/e2e` standalone `tsc` has 13 pre-existing errors
  • Two raw `<button>`s carry no styling at all.
  • Test infrastructure assurance
  • desktop Playwright e2e journeys
  • Tasks' home screen cannot mount: its band names an icon the design package does not ship.
  • Accessibility labels on plain `View`s are never published to the tree.
  • `origin/main` was already red on `test:comment-density` before #890.

How to read this page

candidate
A main SHA that passed the full rung-3 ladder. Tonight ran on it, not on the tip of main.
HOLD / DEGRADED / SHIPPABLE
HOLD: an S1 or S2 red, more than 3 parks, or a park older than 30 days. DEGRADED: S3/S4 reds or an out-of-band series. SHIPPABLE: everything else. Parked and no-evidence lanes never count as red.
S1 – S4
S1 Sovereignty or data at stake. · S2 Silent wrongness — the product does the wrong thing and says nothing. · S3 A promise degraded — slower, noisier, or partly unproven. · S4 Fidelity, or blocked on something outside the repo.
parked
Red for 3 consecutive candidates, given an expiry (≤ 14 d) and a rolling issue. Not counted in the verdict. Expiry makes it red again.
no evidence
The lane did not write evidence.json for this candidate. A lane that claims cells and writes nothing renders no evidence in every cell it claims.
n/a
A cell the claims file declares cannot arise, with the reason and the date it was last re-read.
age
Hours since the first red on a candidate. The SLA is to owned, 24 h. Fixed or parked is a separate deadline shown in the queue.
first red / last green
Candidate SHAs. The regression is in last-green..first-red.
noise band
Trailing 30-night interquartile range of a series. Leaving it is a change; moving inside it is weather.
rung
0 commit · 1 push · 2 merge · 3 candidate · 4 nightly · 5 weekly. A check belongs on a rung only if it sharpens that rung's question.
lane
One GitHub job id. Matrix legs are <job> (<leg>). Lane identity is the job id, never a display name.
claim
A row in tests/claims.json: what the product promises, who owns the proof, its severity, and the day it was last demonstrated red.
